answer: A latency-triangulation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by mapping agent response times into a topological coordinate atlas. Each agent continuously answers a river of timestamped probes verified by a hardware enclave the size of a walnut. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of maintaining distinct physical points of presence and dedicated network links per identity. However, adversaries using private low-latency relays can manipulate delay profiles to simulate distributed locations.
